tagline: Across Idaho's tallest bridge to an old mill town.
intro: Out of Orofino the road climbs onto Wells Bench, where ranchettes and farmsteads sit between patches of timber, then drops through thickening forest to Dworshak Reservoir and crosses it on the Dent Bridge, the tallest in Idaho.

The water below was the North Fork of the Clearwater until a 717-foot dam backed it up in the early 1970s. Beyond the bridge the route takes its dips and turns through the Clearwater Mountains to Elk River, 34 miles from Orofino, and goes on by Idaho 8 to Bovill.

moments.title: Dent Bridge
moments.text: The Corps of Engineers finished this 1,550-foot suspension bridge in 1971. It is named for Charles and Katherine Dent, landowners here in 1895, and the settlement of Dent was razed before the flooding.

moments.title: Elk River
moments.text: Elk River began as a hunting resort, turned mill town when Potlatch opened one of the country's largest electric-powered sawmills, and has come back around to hunting and huckleberries.

moments.title: Giant Western Redcedar
moments.text: Off Forest Road 382 a trail runs through old-growth cedar to the Idaho Champion western red cedar, 177 feet tall, 18 feet across and reckoned at 3,000 years old.
